key_insight: AAMFM is a multimodal foundation model that learns antibody sequence-structure representations conditioned on antigen context, with explicit epitope-aware interaction modeling for functional antibody design.
engineering_relevance: The method provides a practical route to design antibodies targeted to specific antigens, which can improve hit generation and reduce trial-and-error in therapeutic discovery pipelines.
method: Encodes antibody sequences and structures in a shared latent space.
Injects antigen geometry and epitope annotations through a cross-modal adapter.
Fine-tunes with Calibrated Direct Preference Optimization (Cal-DPO) using structural preference signals.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments showing state-of-the-art performance in functional antibody design across antigen-specific evaluation settings.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on the quality of antigen geometry, epitope annotations, and the strength of the structural prior used to generate preference signals.
paper_title: Antigen-specific Antibody Multi-modal Foundation Model for Functional Antibody Design
